# CR-006 — Gift-commerce customer profile fields / ฟิลด์โปรไฟล์ลูกค้าสำหรับธุรกิจของขวัญ

**Status:** approved (Boss, 2026-08-09) · **Mode:** DDD
**Plan ref:** SmartGift `docs/implementation-plan-2026-08-09.md` §5 (ZUMP01 Phase 3) · **Design ref:** `smart-crm-design-2026-08-08.md` §5

## Problem / ปัญหา

SmartGift sells corporate gifts: **3,354 of its 3,569 customers are นิติบุคคล (juristic persons)**.
The CRM has no place to record who the buying organisation is, what industry it is in, or which
occasions it buys for — all of which drive the actual sales motion (New Year gifts, retirement,
anniversaries). Nor is there any notion of account size beyond raw LTV.
Zuri ไม่มีที่เก็บ "ลูกค้าเป็นบริษัทอะไร อยู่อุตสาหกรรมไหน ซื้อในโอกาสใด" ซึ่งเป็นแกนของการขายของขวัญองค์กร

## Two decisions that shape this CR / การตัดสินใจสองข้อ

**1. Account tier is COMPUTED, never stored.** The design doc's provisional rule (LTV ≥ 500k ⇒
enterprise) is a threshold over a number the system already computes. Storing it would create a
value that silently goes stale the moment an order lands — the same class of defect as CR-005's
`ENROLLED` literal. `accountTier` is therefore derived inside the Customer-360 service from LTV,
with the thresholds in **one** named table, and returned by the profile API. No column, no
migration for it, no backfill.
⚠️ **Not to be confused with the existing `Customer.membershipTier`** (default `MEMBER`, surfaced
only in CSV export) — that is a loyalty tier and is **not touched** by this CR. The spec names the
new one `accountTier` precisely so the two never blur.

**2. Stated facts must be protected from AI enrichment.** The new fields live on `CustomerProfile`,
which today is written by the AI enrichment path (`inferenceCount`/`lastInferredAt`,
`customerProfileRepo.upsert`). A human typing "บริษัท จีเอ็มเอ็ม ทีวี จำกัด" must never be
overwritten by an inference run. The repo therefore gets **two disjoint field allowlists** —
`STATED_FIELDS` (human-writable only) and `INFERRED_FIELDS` (enrichment-writable only) — and each
write path may touch only its own set.

## Change / การแก้

| # | Piece | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Prisma schema** — `CustomerProfile` | Additive, all nullable/defaulted (no backfill, no tenant impact): `companyName String? @map("company_name")` · `industry String? @map("industry")` · `occasionPref String[] @default([]) @map("occasion_pref")` (array, matching the existing `motivation String[]` on this model — a customer buys for more than one occasion). **No `tier` column** (decision 1). |
| 2 | **Migration** | Hand-written SQL migration under `prisma/migrations/<timestamp>_gift_commerce_profile_fields/migration.sql`, following the style of the most recent migration in that directory. `ALTER TABLE "customer_profiles" ADD COLUMN ...` — additive only, no data change, safe to run on a live table. |
| 3 | **`customerProfileRepo`** | Introduce `STATED_FIELDS = ['companyName','industry','occasionPref']` and `INFERRED_FIELDS` (the existing inferred set). `upsert(customerId, incoming)` — the enrichment path — filters to `INFERRED_FIELDS` and must **not** write stated fields or clear them. New `updateStated(customerId, incoming)` filters to `STATED_FIELDS`, does not touch `inferenceCount`/`lastInferredAt`. Both scoped through the customer's tenant by the caller (route resolves the customer first). |
| 4 | **`accountTier`** — `src/lib/customerTier.js` (new) | `ACCOUNT_TIERS` table, ordered, each `{ key, label, labelTh, minLtv }`: `tier3_smb` (0), `tier2_corporate` (100_000), `tier1_enterprise` (500_000). `resolveAccountTier(ltv)` → the highest tier whose `minLtv` is met; never throws, handles null/NaN as `tier3_smb`. A file-top comment records that these thresholds are **PROVISIONAL, pending the business owner's real criteria** (design doc §5) so nobody treats them as settled. |
| 5 | **Customer-360 service** — `src/lib/services/customerInsightService.js` | `computeProfile` additionally returns `accountTier: resolveAccountTier(ltv)` (the descriptor, not just a key) and `stated: { companyName, industry, occasionPref }` read from `CustomerProfile`. Existing returned fields (`ltv`, `frequency`, `recency`, `segment`) are **unchanged** — the `segment` VIP/PREMIUM/CUSTOMER logic stays exactly as is. |
| 6 | **API** — `src/app/api/customers/[id]/profile/route.js` | Keep `GET` (now includes `accountTier` + `stated`). Add `PATCH` with `{ domain: 'customers', action: 'W' }`: body may contain only `companyName`/`industry`/`occasionPref`; anything else → `400` naming the accepted fields (never a silent drop). Resolve the customer within the caller's tenant first → `404` if absent. `occasionPref` must be an array of non-empty strings; trim and cap at 20 entries. No `getPrisma` import (repo-pattern guardrail). |
| 7 | **UI** — Customer-360 card | Surface the three stated fields plus the computed `accountTier` badge on the customer detail surface (`src/components/crm/CustomerDetail.jsx` and/or `src/app/(dashboard)/crm/[id]/page.jsx` — follow whichever already renders the 360 data; do not restructure the page). Stated fields are editable inline where the page already has an edit affordance; if it has none, render read-only and leave a comment naming the follow-up. Thai-first labels: บริษัท / อุตสาหกรรม / โอกาสที่ซื้อ / ระดับบัญชี. |
| 8 | **PDPA** | No new erasure work needed — `consentRepo.eraseCustomer` already deletes the whole `CustomerProfile` row, so the new columns are covered. Add one line to `docs/specs/CR-003-consent-erasure.md` §3 noting the profile row now also carries firmographics, so the coverage is deliberate rather than accidental. |
| 9 | **Tests** | `resolveAccountTier` boundary table (0 / 99_999 / 100_000 / 499_999 / 500_000 / null / NaN). `customerProfileRepo`: **enrichment `upsert` cannot write or clear stated fields; `updateStated` cannot touch inferred fields or the inference counters** (this is the guard the whole CR rests on). Profile route: `PATCH` happy path, unknown field → 400, non-array `occasionPref` → 400, cross-tenant id → 404, `GET` includes `accountTier` + `stated`. `computeProfile` still returns the same `segment` for an unchanged input (regression). |

## Acceptance Criteria / เกณฑ์ยอมรับ

- **AC1** An AI enrichment run (`upsert`) on a customer with a human-entered `companyName` leaves
  that value byte-identical, and a `updateStated` call leaves `inferenceCount`/`lastInferredAt`
  and every inferred field untouched. (The core regression of this CR.)
- **AC2** `GET /api/customers/[id]/profile` returns `accountTier` (key + label) and `stated`;
  `ltv`, `frequency`, `recency`, `segment` are unchanged for the same input.
- **AC3** `PATCH` accepts only the three stated fields; any other key returns 400 listing the
  accepted fields; a customer outside the caller's tenant returns 404.
- **AC4** `resolveAccountTier` maps LTV to the documented boundaries, and `null`/`NaN`/negative
  fall to `tier3_smb` rather than throwing.
- **AC5** The migration is additive-only and `npx prisma validate` passes; no existing tenant's
  data or behaviour changes (all new columns nullable/defaulted).
- **AC6** `npm run lint` + targeted vitest + `npm run test:scripts` green.

## Out of scope / นอกขอบเขต

Any change to `Customer.membershipTier` (loyalty tier — different concept) · the `segment`
VIP/PREMIUM/CUSTOMER thresholds · importing company names from the local SmartGift dataset (PII
stays local per the design doc — these fields are filled in by staff or by future LINE/LIFF
capture) · industry as a validated enum (free text for now; a controlled list needs the business
owner's taxonomy) · automations or segments keyed on the new fields (CR-009) · confirming the real
tier thresholds — **`ACCOUNT_TIERS` is provisional and must be reviewed by the business owner
before any pricing, reporting or automation depends on it**.

## Rollout / การปล่อย

Additive migration; deploy order within Phase 3 is independent of CR-005. Apply with the
repository's migration runbook (`db:push:LOCAL_ONLY` in dev). Nothing reads the new fields until
staff fill them in, so there is no behaviour change on deploy.
